findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting or category is absent
findings.body: The migration unconditionally dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] and, on line 15, execute(...)[0]['value']. On a fresh install or any site that never saved embed_category/uncategorized_category_id in site_settings, [0] is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError and cannot complete, blocking deployment/upgrades.

findings.title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim without normalization and via string interpolation
findings.body: Legacy SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts values could contain values such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (as existing specs used). This raw INSERT stores them verbatim, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation stripping of scheme/path, so record_for_host (which compares against URI#host) will never match those migrated rows and embedding silently breaks for them. Interpolating h directly into SQL also breaks on quotes and allows SQL injection through a crafted setting value.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: self.host.sub! is called unconditionally. Creating an EmbeddableHost with no host (e.g. an admin API POST missing embeddable_host[host], or EmbeddableHost.new.valid?) raises NoMethodError for nil instead of failing validates_format_of gracefully with a validation error the controller can render.

findings.title: Update/destroy of nonexistent host raises NoMethodError instead of 404
findings.body: update looks up EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes it to save_host, and destroy (line 15-16) calls host.destroy, without checking for nil. A stale UI row or a request with a bad id therefore returns a 500 NoMethodError rather than a handled not-found/error response.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host makes category selection nondeterministic
findings.body: host has no uniqueness validation (and the migration creates no unique index). Admins can create two rows for the same hostname with different categories; record_for_host then uses .first with no ordering, so TopicEmbed.import can arbitrarily pick either category_id for new embedded topics depending on database return order.

findings.title: Plural embedded hydration inserts undefined entries and drops unmatched ids
findings.body: In the new _ids branch, obj[k].map returns whatever _lookupSubType returns, which is undefined when the subtype collection is absent from the payload root or the id is not in it (e.g. the special-cased category lookup returning undefined). The resulting plural array contains undefined elements (later code expecting models will fail), and unlike the singular branch it deletes obj[k] unconditionally (line 201), discarding the original ids even when nothing was hydrated.

findings.title: Edit action crashes for hosts without a category
findings.body: edit() does this.get('host.category.id') with no guard. A host whose category was deleted (belongs_to does not prevent orphan category_id, and category_id can also be hydrated as undefined by the store) has category == null/undefined, so clicking Edit throws a TypeError and the row can never be edited or fixed in the UI.

findings.title: Category and embeddable_host fabricators are placed in each other's files
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category. Tests still pass because all fabricator files are loaded, but maintainers editing or selectively loading the conventionally named file will modify/load the wrong definitions.
